title: Lane file
description: One lane of a project's plan record. The filename is the lane and sequence order is the human ranking within it.

lane.description: Must equal the file basename so a pasted fragment remains self-describing.

stories.description: Ordered highest-priority first. Position is the ranking; there is no priority field.

id.description: The title's slug, plus at most a qualifying postfix where that slug was taken. The id is the story document's filename stem. No consumer parses its interior.

type.description: The kind of work and the condition for the worked-example gate.

points.description: Units of irreducible human judgment. Work above 3 must split.

needs.description: Ids that must be closed before this story is eligible.

epic.description: Id of one epic document at <plan zone>/epics/<id>.md, where the zone is the directory this file lives two levels below. Ids are unique across stories and epics alike, so one id names one thing. Single-valued and never a sequencing fact.

tags.description: Free board labels. Nothing gates on a tag.

branch.description: The code branch carrying this entry's work — an explicit cross-reference, because plan and code no longer share commits. Opaque to every check beyond shape: the record cannot verify another repository.

outcome.description: Required in closed.yml and forbidden elsewhere.

closed.description: Required in closed.yml and forbidden elsewhere; used to derive velocity.

delivered.description: The commit that delivered the work, as its identifier in the host's version control. Meaningful in closed.yml only, like outcome and closed; the same standing as branch — stated, searchable, never verified.

succeeded_by.description: Required when outcome is reshaped and forbidden otherwise.

summary.description: One capped paragraph restating what this entry is, so a lane file answers without a file read per row. The story document stays the source of truth; this is a restatement of it and never a second specification. Double-quote it: an unquoted scalar carrying a colon is ambiguous under YAML. One line, no leading or trailing whitespace, because the record is parsed by a flat canonical subset.

note.description: Free prose about the entry's handling rather than about its subject — why it is parked, who is waiting on it, what a reader should know before picking it up. What the work is belongs in summary. Nothing parses it.
